values: Materials and setup｜A1—A5 are all editor-designed fictional recycling programs, not real collection instructions

You are responsible for the paper coordination of three curbside collection routes R1—R3 and one drop-off point D1. Plan 30 minutes: 5 minutes reading constraints, 20 minutes scheduling and reconciliation, 5 minutes writing escalation and handoff.

A1｜Tuesday 09:00—12:00: R1 is served by driver A and technician B in the east zone, with a planned collection of 1,200 kg; R2 is served by driver C and technician D in the west zone, with a plan of 900 kg; R3 is served by driver E and technician F in the north zone, with a plan of 700 kg. D1 is open 09:00—17:00, with records kept by attendant G. All of the above is fictional.

A2｜At 11:45 the actual collection records arrived: R1 1,160 kg, R2 880 kg, and R3 700 kg. The preliminary total is 2,740 kg; the planned total is 2,800 kg, a difference of 60 kg. The planned amount is not a guaranteed receivable, and the cause of the difference must be investigated.

A3｜The processor receiving receipts are R1 1,160 kg, R2 850 kg, and R3 700 kg, totaling 2,710 kg. The collection record for R2 and the receiving receipt differ by 30 kg; D1 separately received 180 kg of cardboard that day, but there is no transfer receipt yet, so it cannot be counted as delivered to the processor.

A4｜At 10:12, the driver of R2 reported a vehicle reversing blind spot interleaving with pedestrians near a drop-off point; at the same time a resident complained about a missed collection at a west zone stop. The coordinator first pauses the affected R2 near-station loading/unloading or rerouting actions and notifies the on-site safety supervisor and the driver to verify the location and protection, while the complaint is checked against the address and completion records first, without promising unapproved supplementary collection.

A5｜Authorization chain: the coordinator may log, verify tickets, and propose route adjustments; the on-site safety supervisor confirms whether the hazard is resolved, the dispatch supervisor approves rerouting or supplementary collection, and the processor confirms correction receipts. The prompt contains no approval to resume or reroute, and no D1 transfer receipt. The handoff should preserve the open status.

subject.summary: Recycling coordinators supervise municipal or corporate curbside collection and drop-off recycling programs: they arrange routes and staffing, verify collection and delivery records, handle service requests, train workers, and coordinate safety and compliance. Specific budget, contract, equipment, and on-site disposal authority depends on the employer and location.
